nodes.label: A shape check alone cannot reject an opaque hash; a namespace allowlist is what rejects it
nodes.norm_label: a shape check alone cannot reject an opaque hash a namespace allowlist is what rejects it
nodes.summary: record_ticket_link accepted anything containing a colon. The quote below states why the obvious fix is not enough: both halves of the counterexample are alphanumeric, so a character-shape test passes it and only the namespace half rejects it.
nodes.rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar/2026-10-01 - author-r5-validation-patch [ses_f0a7762c0ffemYT9pqFsuNc6fX].md:L6473] "1. **`record_ticket_link` (`database/ticket_links.rs:18`)** accepts anything with a `:` — `"foo:bar"` links successfully, violating the opaque-hash contract (both sides must be `opaque_source_id` output, hashed at the Tauri boundary per `stats_cmds.rs:362-363`). Shape-only checks can't reject `"foo:bar"` (both halves are alnum); only `validate_event`'s **namespace allowlist + char-shape** combo (`analytics_v2/events.rs:25-53`) does. Mirror that, per-side: event sources reuse the 13 analytics namespaces, ticket hashes allow only `"ticket"`."

nodes.label: Detecting a missing migration by string-matching "no such column" is fragile; match the rusqlite SqliteFailure extended code instead
nodes.norm_label: detecting a missing migration by string matching no such column is fragile match the rusqlite sqlitefailure extended code instead
nodes.summary: Reused id: chunk-rem-101 carries this claim from the audit that raised it. This session independently reaches it from the hardening side and adds the consequence the audit did not state: the substring also swallows every other SqliteFailure whose text happens to match.
nodes.rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar/2026-10-01 - author-r5-validation-patch [ses_f0a7762c0ffemYT9pqFsuNc6fX].md:L6474] "2. **`is_group_tagged_for_research` (`database/groups.rs:338-345`)** sniffs `"no such column"` via `to_string().contains` — locale/message-fragile, and it also swallows any *other* `SqliteFailure` whose text happens to match. nodes.label: A missing column is detected by a pragma_table_info pre-check, because the linked SQLCipher build has no usable MISSING_COLUMN extended code
nodes.norm_label: a missing column is detected by a pragmatableinfo pre check because the linked sqlcipher build has no usable missingcolumn extended code
nodes.summary: This session was told to match the extended code and found the instruction was not executable on this build, then delivered a different mechanism instead. The three quotes are the finding, the consequence that forced the choice, and the reason the pragma form is not an ad-hoc invention.
rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar/2026-10-01 - author-r5-validation-patch [ses_f0a7762c0ffemYT9pqFsuNc6fX].md:L6604] "- **No usable extended code exists in this stack.** Upstream's `SQLITE_ERROR_MISSING_COLUMN = (SQLITE_ERROR|(7<<8)) = 1793` is **absent from both vendored headers**: `sqlite3/sqlite3.h:500-505` and `sqlcipher/bindgen_bundled_version.rs:64-69` stop at `SQLITE_ERROR_UNABLE = 1537` (`6<<8`); no `MISSING_COLUMN` string anywhere in either tree. The linked SQLCipher therefore reports "no such column" as bare primary code 1 (`extended_code == 1`, `ErrorCode::Unknown`)."

[05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar/2026-10-01 - author-r5-validation-patch [ses_f0a7762c0ffemYT9pqFsuNc6fX].md:L6605] "- **Consequence**: matching `extended_code == 1793` (or any named `MISSING_COLUMN` constant — it wouldn't compile) would be **dead code that never fires**, regressing the unmigrated-DB path from `Ok(false)` to `Err`. Matching `code == Unknown && extended == 1` without the message is worse — it swallows *all* generic SQL errors (typos included). The pragma pre-check above is the only correct "no string matching" fix on this build; if the vendor ever rebases SQLCipher past upstream 3.44, revisit."

[05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar/2026-10-01 - author-r5-validation-patch [ses_f0a7762c0ffemYT9pqFsuNc6fX].md:L6570] "(Pragma pre-check is the established idiom: `schema.rs:552-559`, `schema_migrations.rs:30-63`.)"

nodes.label: NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 makes the documented NULL read-branch unrepresentable
nodes.norm_label: not null default 0 makes the documented null read branch unrepresentable
nodes.summary: A doc comment described a NULL path the schema forbids, and the read type chosen would error on NULL rather than yield false. The two quotes are the correction and the evidence it was checked against.
rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar/2026-10-01 - author-r5-validation-patch [ses_f0a7762c0ffemYT9pqFsuNc6fX].md:L6475] "3. **Doc overclaim (`groups.rs:325-328`)**: says "NULL/0 reads as `Ok(false)`", but the column is `INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0` (`schema.rs:36`, `schema_migrations.rs:108`), so NULL is unrepresentable and `row.get::<i64>` on NULL would `Err` (`InvalidColumnType`), not yield `false`. Correct the doc, not behavior."
